summary.headline: Flomic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps to 9.34%, but PAT fell to INR2.06 crore from INR2.98 crore.
summary.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 18.4% YoY to INR120 crore, with management attributing most of the growth to higher freight rates rather than volume (shipments up roughly 6-7%). EBITDA rose about 68% to INR11.21 crore and margin improved to 9.34% from 6.59%. PBT turned positive at INR2.73 crore from a loss of INR3.3 crore a year earlier, while PAT was INR2.06 crore versus INR2.98 crore last year. Management said a one-time INR28 lakh lease-related benefit was included, and it cited branch closures, manpower cost reduction and an AI-based back-office system from 1 July as margin levers.</overview>

segments.name: Air & Sea Import Forwarding
segments.commentary: Revenue INR40 crore in Q1; management said all segments improved YoY, but no prior-year split was given.

segments.name: Sea Export
segments.commentary: Revenue around INR33.39 crore in Q1; management said ocean exports are the main incremental profit pool while freight rates are rising.

segments.name: Air Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR22 crore in Q1; management said some cargo has shifted from ocean to air, adding to this segment.

segments.name: Warehousing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR18 crore in Q1; around 15% of revenue now, with a stated gross margin of 15-16% (15-20% range), targeted at 17-18% and then about 20% of contribution.

segments.name: Air & Sea Import Clearance
segments.commentary: Revenue INR7.42 crore in Q1; management did not give further detail.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth momentum to continue for three to four quarters, but gave no numerical FY27 target.
Management expects ocean and air export benefits to last at least two to three more quarters while freight rates stay elevated.
Management said freight rate-driven growth may not be long-term sustainable.
Warehousing share of revenue is targeted to rise to 17-18% and then about 20%.
Management expects operating margins to improve further from corrective actions, higher freight rates and AI-led cost reduction.
Management says it will stay asset-light, with warehousing expansion mainly leased and customer-backed.
capex_capacity: Warehousing expansion will be selective, leased and customer-backed rather than driven by square footage.
Project cargo vertical is being built with a newly hired team; management called it higher margin but higher execution risk.
AI-based application (back-office documentation, quotation-to-billing) started from 1 July 2026; the company handled about 42,000 shipments last year, previously with manual file creation.
Priorities for FY27 include CFS and air cargo capabilities, presence across key Indian hubs and selectively overseas.
No capex amount or capacity figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth was mainly price-driven: shipment volumes rose about 6-7% YoY, with the rest from freight rates, which rose sharply on geopolitical volatility.
Middle East disruption reduced export cargo volumes, per management.
Management targets mid-sized customers and avoids both very large corporates and small startups, citing margin and payment risk.
Project cargo demand cited from oil and gas, aerospace, energy, pharma cold chain and solar; exports mainly to Africa, imports from Germany and China.
Management did not disclose the customer count beyond an analyst's reference to about 5,000 active customers.

qa_highlights.question: How does management view FY27 revenue growth for Flomic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects revenue to be better on higher freight rates, with momentum for three to four quarters, but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and margin profile of the project logistics business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described oversized, dimensional project cargo needing special equipment and permits, with higher margins than routine freight forwarding and higher execution risk; no revenue scale was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipment growth was about 6-7% YoY; the remainder came from freight rate increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin after excluding the one-time INR28 lakh benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT margin was still significantly higher YoY even after excluding the INR28 lakh, and that manpower cost has already been reduced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warehousing margin and growth potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said warehousing gross margin is 15-16% (15-20% range), with Ind AS 116 inflating reported segment margin because rent on leased assets is excluded; share of revenue is to rise to about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What annual savings are expected from closing loss-making branches?
qa_highlights.answer: No savings figure was given; management said closed branches were non-performing and located where the company lacked customers.

risks_watch: PAT declined YoY to INR2.06 crore despite EBITDA growth of ~68%, implying higher depreciation, interest or tax; the call did not explain the gap.
Growth is mainly freight-rate driven and management itself said it may not be sustainable; volumes grew only ~6-7%.
Receivable days of 56-57 remain above the company's own 30-60 day comfort range's upper end only partly; any slip raises interest cost.
Execution risk in project cargo and warehousing expansion, and the new AI system's rollout from 1 July 2026.
Middle East disruption is reducing export cargo volumes.
Q1 results include a one-time INR28 lakh lease-related benefit; check the underlying run-rate next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margin trajectory and the company's integrated model, but vague on numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 revenue or margin targets and gave no capex or branch-savings figures. Answers on the freight-rate tailwind were candid that it may not be durable.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margin also improved to 9.34% from 6.59%, effective increase of 275 basis points.
We are not chasing only turnover. Our focus is on gross profit, margins, working capital discipline, and quality customers and better systems.
The freight growth sustainability may not be very long term.
